comments.text:
I can see the arguments behind - I want to experience things now, you can't take it with you, but, and there's obviously a but, that's fine _IF_ you have the cash to pay for it in full. If you've got to get a loan or use a credit card to offset the payment, you can't afford to do it.

I got made redundant 9 years ago, I was 53. I had been debt free for 14 years prior to that and working 8-10 hours OT every week and banking that money. The company were helpful, trying to find people new jobs, my answer to HR when asked what I wanted to do was: retire ASAP. 
I could have looked for a new job, but I took a different route. I looked at my savings and worked out a monthly budget I could afford until I could draw social security. I then looked at where I could live that fit that monthly budget. I made a list and researched where ticked the most boxes, sold all my stuff, immigrated to SE Asia, and retired.

The people I worked with, friends, family and neighbors were all shocked when instead of job hunting I immigrated and retired. I live a quiet, very simple, stress free life paid for by over a decade of small amounts of OT, zero debt, living well within my means, and doing without the consumer shit nobody really needs.
You want to know what's infinitely better than working to pay off your debt, and taking a couple of weeks holiday a year? Retiring at 53, not working, not having any debts and having 52 weeks holiday a year. 


It's not easy to do when you're young, but I think people need to balance the meaningless things they want now against what they'll want in the future. By the age of 33 the novelty of working 50 weeks a year had worn off, and I set out to end my debt cycle and plan an escape. I didn't plan to retire at 53 and I certainly didn't plan to immigrate, but I don't regret either. 
We don't know how long we have on this earth, so destroying yourself working 80 hours a week for 40 years only to die 2 weeks after you retire at 68 seems insane, better to live modestly, make do and mend, then retire young.

Good channel, I hope some people listen to your comments, reject consumerism, and get to retire young and enjoy their later years.
